docs.title: cvprism
docs.text:
Work on many machines. Get many CVs. Write none of them by hand.

You pick up new skills nearly every day: a library, an API, a model, a field method. Your CV gets updated once a year, from memory, as one generic document. cvprism closes that gap.

  • It captures skills, methods and measurable results from your Claude Code sessions, git commits, project files and one-line notes. It never captures code, data or file contents.
  • It deduplicates what it already knows, so you get one card when you level up, not a hundred.
  • It syncs cards from every computer to one hub over git, Google Drive/OneDrive/Dropbox, a USB stick or Syncthing, with no conflicts by design.
  • It builds CVs for a role or a specific job posting as PDF, DOCX and Markdown. Every bullet cites the evidence behind it, and invented numbers are rejected by code.

    accDescr: Work on several computers becomes evidence cards, which sync to a hub that builds role-specific CVs.
    work["Your work on any computer"] --> cards["Evidence cards"] --> sync["Sync: git, Drive, USB, Syncthing"] --> hub["Hub"]
    hub --> a["Academic CV"]
    hub --> i["Industry CV"]
    hub --> j["CV for this job posting"]

docs.title: See it in 30 seconds
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/sayantanonfire/cvprism.git && cd cvprism
./start.sh --name demo --role hub --vault ~/cvprism-vault --yes   # Windows: start.bat ...
cvprism demo --out ~/cvprism-demo

cvprism demo builds three role CVs and one job-tailored CV for a synthetic person, fully offline. Open cv.pdf, then evidence.md to see which card backs each bullet, and gaps.md to see what the job asks for that the evidence does not cover.

docs.text:
Status: Phase 0 draft for review. Nothing here is implemented yet. Normative words (MUST, SHOULD, MAY) follow RFC 2119.

cvprism turns ordinary work spread over several computers into evidence cards. It syncs them to one hub machine and builds CVs for specific roles from them. Every CV bullet traces back to at least one card.

docs.title: 🎯 Goals and non-goals
docs.text:
Goals

  1. Capture methodology, skills, tools, techniques and measurable results continuously, with no user effort beyond an optional one-line log.
  2. Keep state in plain, human-readable files. No database, no server, no dependency on any Claude account.
  3. Sync from any number of devices into one hub over interchangeable transports, without conflicts.
  4. Compile tailored CVs (academic, industry, applied-AI, domain) where every claim cites evidence.
  5. Stay cheap: deterministic code does filtering and dedup, and the LLM sees only small, pre-filtered inputs.

Non-goals (v1)

  • Capturing raw data, file contents, source code or client data. This is a hard rule (see SECURITY_PRIVACY.md).
  • Real-time sync, multi-user vaults, a hosted service or a GUI CV editor.
  • A native LAN server (cvprism hub serve is on the post-v1 roadmap; see ADR-006).
  • Writing our own CV typesetter (ADR-010).

docs.title: Local state vs vault
docs.text:
Two storage locations are kept strictly apart.

Location Contents Synced? ~/.cvprism/ (platform data dir, via platformdirs) device.yaml, outbox/<device-id>/*.jsonl, queue/, counters.json, registry.cache.json, adapter cursors, logs No. Only the outbox is replicated, by adapters Vault (hub: a real directory; spokes: reached only through adapters) inbox/<device-id>/, cards.jsonl, registry.json, profile.yaml, roles/, market/, hub.json, vault.json Yes, through adapters

The outbox lives on local disk first, so a card exists durably on the device that captured it before any transport is involved. Adapters only ever copy outbox files into inbox/<device-id>/ at the transport. Spokes never hold a full vault. That keeps the career history of a whole vault off a lost laptop or USB stick, except where the user chooses a full-vault transport.

docs.title: Capture to card (every device)
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    accTitle: Capture Pipeline
    accDescr: Signals from four sources are queued, reduced to a sanitised digest in code, extracted by Claude, redacted, and passed through the novelty filter, which either writes a card to the outbox or increments a local counter.

    src_claude["Claude Code SessionEnd"]
    src_git["git post-commit"]
    src_watch["Folder watcher"]
    src_manual["cvprism log / /cv-log"]

    queue_q[("📥 File queue")]
    reduce_r["✂️ Reducer (code)<br/>drop file contents,<br/>tool output, data"]
    extract_e["🤖 Extractor<br/>claude -p + JSON schema"]
    redact_r["🛡️ Redactor<br/>deny-list, aliases, secrets"]
    validate_v{"Schema valid?"}
    novelty_n{"Novel?<br/>new skill / higher depth<br/>/ new result"}
    outbox_o[("📤 Outbox JSONL<br/>append-only")]
    counter_c[("🔢 counters.json")]
    reject_r[("🗑️ rejects.log")]

    src_claude --> queue_q
    src_git --> queue_q
    src_watch --> queue_q
    src_manual -->|"skips reducer"| extract_e
    queue_q --> reduce_r --> extract_e --> redact_r --> validate_v
    validate_v -->|"no"| reject_r
    validate_v -->|"yes"| novelty_n
    novelty_n -->|"yes"| outbox_o
    novelty_n -->|"no"| counter_c

    classDef store fill:#f3e8ff,stroke:#7c3aed,stroke-width:2px,color:#3b0764
    classDef step fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px,color:#1e3a5f
    class queue_q,outbox_o,counter_c,reject_r store
    class reduce_r,extract_e,redact_r step

Key properties:

  • Hooks only enqueue. A Claude Code SessionEnd hook MUST return within milliseconds. Extraction runs later in the worker. This also stops the extractor's own claude -p session from triggering capture recursively: the worker sets CVPRISM_EXTRACTING=1, and the hook exits immediately when it sees that variable.
  • The reducer runs before the LLM. The digest keeps user prompts (truncated), tool names, file extensions, package names, command verbs and commit subjects. It drops file contents, tool outputs, diffs and data. This is both the privacy boundary and the token budget, capped by extraction.max_input_tokens (default 6k).
  • Manual entries go straight to the extractor, which normalises them into the market-facing card form. With --raw they skip the LLM entirely, so cvprism log works offline and with no Claude installed.
  • Missing metrics are never invented. If the text implies a result but gives no number, r is null and flags contains needs_metric. cvprism review lists these for the user to fill in.

docs.text:
flowchart LR

    accDescr: The compiler loads a role profile or JD, filters and scores cards in code, sends a bounded subset with profile facts to Claude to draft cited bullets, enforces citation and metric honesty, then renders via RenderCV and Pandoc.

    role_in["📋 roles/<role>.yaml<br/>or JD → ad-hoc role"]

    render_r["🖨️ RenderCV (PDF)<br/>Pandoc (DOCX/MD)"]
    out_o["📄 build/<role>/<date>/"]
    fail_f["❌ Rejected bullets<br/>+ report"]

    gate_g -->|"pass"| render_r --> out_o
    gate_g -->|"fail, 1 retry then drop"| fail_f

    classDef step fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,stroke-width:2px,color:#1e3a5f

The honesty gate is deterministic code, not a prompt instruction (ADR-009). It:

  1. Rejects any bullet without [c_…] citations, or citing IDs not in cards.jsonl.
  2. Extracts every number (including %, x, ranges and written-out numbers) from the bullet. Each one MUST appear in a cited card's r or in profile.yaml. Otherwise the bullet is rejected.
  3. Writes build/<role>/<date>/evidence.md, a bullet-to-card trace you can audit before sending a CV.

docs.title: 🧩 Topology and hub lifecycle
docs.text:
• Exactly one hub per vault. Its identity lives in vault/hub.json as {hub_device_id, epoch}.
  • cvprism hub promote on a new device increments epoch and becomes authoritative for hub-owned files. Spokes accept registry.json only from the highest (epoch, rev).
  • A demoted hub that comes back online sees a higher epoch in hub.json and stops writing hub-owned files. It keeps its own inbox, so no data is lost.
  • Spokes never talk to each other, and a spoke never writes outside inbox/<own-device-id>/ on any transport.
stateDiagram-v2
    accTitle: Device Role Lifecycle
    accDescr: A device is installed as a spoke or a hub. A spoke can be promoted to hub, which bumps the epoch, and the old hub becomes a spoke when it observes the higher epoch.

    [*] --> Spoke: install (role=spoke)
    [*] --> Hub: install (role=hub, new vault)
    Spoke --> Hub: cvprism hub promote (epoch+1)
    Hub --> Spoke: sees higher epoch in hub.json
    Hub --> Hub: merge / publish (rev+1)

docs.title: 💥 Failure modes
docs.text: # Failure Effect Mitigation F1 No adapter reachable (offline, no USB) Cards accumulate locally The outbox is durable storage. Cursors push everything once any adapter returns. cvprism status shows the backlog F2 Partial file at the transport (Drive mid-upload, USB yanked) Last line truncated Writers always end lines with \n. The hub ignores an unterminated last line and gets it on the next pull F3 Synced-folder conflict copy (2026-11 (1).jsonl, …conflicted copy…) Duplicate files The hub globs and unions all *.jsonl in each inbox dir. Content-hash IDs make the union idempotent F4 Same achievement captured on two devices Duplicate cards Identical canonical fields give the same id and are deduped at merge. Near-duplicates (different wording, same facts) are caught by the canonical-field ID because free text is excluded (ADR-002) F5 Two devices both believe they are the hub (split brain) Competing cards.jsonl / registry.json Epoch in hub.json. Lower-epoch hub output is ignored and the lower-epoch hub self-demotes. cards.jsonl is always reproducible from the inboxes, so nothing is lost F6 Stale registry on a spoke Spoke emits a card the hub already knows Harmless. The hub dedups by ID and the novelty check is repeated at merge F7 Extractor returns invalid JSON / hallucinated metric Bad card JSON-schema validation and retry once, then reject. Metrics must quote a number present in the digest, otherwise they are nulled and flagged F8 claude CLI missing or not logged in No auto-extraction Jobs stay queued (TTL 30 days), cvprism doctor reports it, and manual --raw logging still works F9 SessionEnd hook recursion Infinite extraction loop CVPRISM_EXTRACTING=1 guard, plus a queue dedup key per transcript path F10 Transcript deleted before the worker runs (Claude Code cleanup) Lost session The worker runs within minutes. Jobs with a missing transcript are dropped and logged. Transcripts are never copied (privacy) F11 Global core.hooksPath hides repo-local hooks Breaks user tooling (husky, pre-commit) The dispatcher chains to $GIT_DIR/hooks/<name> and to any previous global path (ADR-008) F12 Vault accidentally committed to the public code repo Privacy leak The wizard refuses vault paths inside a cvprism checkout. vault.json carries a vault_id. The code repo .gitignore excludes vault/ F13 Two vaults on one transport (two users or test vault) Cross-contamination Every adapter checks vault_id in the transport's vault.json before reading or writing F14 Clock skew between devices Out-of-order timestamps Correctness never depends on time. Month files use device-local capture time. Ordering at the hub is by (t, id) for display only F15 Secret or client name leaks into a card Privacy Redactor deny-list, secret regexes and entropy check before write. Optional review_mode holds cards in pending/ until approved

docs.title: ⚙️ Runtime and platform
docs.text: Concern Choice Language Python ≥ 3.10, one venv in the platform data dir (never on the USB stick) CLI typer File watching watchdog Schemas jsonschema (draft 2020-12); the schemas in cvprism/schemas/ are the single source YAML ruamel.yaml (round-trip, preserves user comments) Login service Windows: per-user HKCU\...\Run value (pythonw -m cvprism agent, no admin); macOS: launchd LaunchAgent; Linux: systemd --user unit, falling back to an XDG autostart .desktop file LLM claude -p --output-format json invoked by subprocess (ADR-007) Rendering RenderCV for PDF, Pandoc for DOCX/MD (ADR-010)

docs.title: ❓ Open questions
docs.text:
These need your decision before or during M1/M2. Each one names the default I would pick.

2026-11-27: M1 started with every default below adopted provisionally (owner said "go ahead"). Any of them can still be overturned. Each is isolated behind config or a single module.

  1. Counters on the hub. Should per-skill usage counters (count, last_seen) reach the hub? They make good evidence ("used daily for 14 months") but are mutable. Default: each device appends a monthly rollup line {"k":"usage", …} to its inbox, which keeps it append-only.
  2. Review before write. Should auto-captured cards go straight to the outbox, or wait in pending/ until approved? Default: straight through, with review_mode: true available. Weekly cvprism review digest.
  3. Extraction model and cost. claude -p uses whichever account is logged in on each device. Should we pin a cheaper model (e.g. Haiku) for extraction via --model? Default: yes, with extraction.model configurable.
  4. Wizard form. TUI or a local browser page for the first run? Default: TUI in M1 (works over SSH, no server), browser page in M6.
  5. Package distribution. Publish to PyPI as cvprism (claim the name now) and have start.sh install from the local checkout or USB? Default: yes to both.
  6. Skill taxonomy seed. Should we seed the registry with an external taxonomy (ESCO, O*NET, Lightcast open skills) for alias normalisation, or grow organically? Default: small hand-curated seed (~300 tech and science skills) plus organic growth. Check licences before adopting ESCO/Lightcast.
  7. Market intel source (M5). Scraping job boards raises terms-of-service problems. Default: the user pastes or saves postings into vault/market/raw/, and cvprism extracts from those. Official APIs come later.
  8. Full-vault transports. Should spokes ever receive cards.jsonl (e.g. to build a CV away from the hub)? Default: no in v1. Only the hub compiles, which keeps the "lost laptop" exposure small.
  9. Card language. English only in v1? Default: yes. Cards carry a lang field reserved for later.
  10. Encryption at rest on transports. Should inbox files on Drive/USB be encrypted (e.g. age)? Default: not in v1. Documented as a known exposure, optional age encryption in M6.
  11. Licence. The repo has Apache-2.0. RenderCV is MIT, and Pandoc is GPL but invoked as a separate binary, not linked. Confirm Apache-2.0 is intended.

docs.title: 🧱 M1: Single machine ✅
docs.text:
Done 2026-11-27. All automated criteria pass in CI (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows × Python 3.10/3.13, plus start-script bootstrap jobs).

Scope: start.sh/start.bat, venv bootstrap, TUI wizard (device name, role, vault path), vault template, cvprism log, card schema and ID, local registry, novelty filter, counters, cvprism status, cvprism doctor.

Acceptance criteria

  1. On a clean machine with Python ≥ 3.10, ./start.sh (or start.bat) creates the venv in the platform data dir and launches the wizard. Finished in < 2 min. (manual on 3 OSes, plus scripted CI)
  2. cvprism log --raw "Built an MCP server exposing HEC-RAS runs" --skill mcp-server-development --depth 3 writes exactly one schema-valid line to outbox/<dev>/YYYY-MM.jsonl.
  3. Running the same command again writes no card and increments counters.json[mcp-server-development].n.
  4. The same command with --depth 4 writes a new depth card. With --result "latency:-40:%" it writes a new result card.
  5. Card IDs are stable across OSes and Python versions (golden-file test over 50 canonical inputs).
  6. The wizard refuses a vault path inside the code checkout.
  7. cvprism log "<text>" (LLM mode) produces a market-phrased card when claude is available, and falls back to --raw with a warning when it is not.

docs.title: 🛰️ M2: Auto-capture 🟡
docs.text:
Implemented 2026-11-27. Criteria 1–6 are automated and passing. Criterion 7 (a real session plus a reboot) needs the owner to run cvprism install on a real machine.

Scope: Claude Code SessionEnd hook installer, global git hook dispatcher with chaining, watcher for opted-in paths, file queue and worker, reducer, extractor prompt and schema, redactor, login service per OS, /cv-log skill.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Installing registers the SessionEnd hook in user-level Claude Code settings without clobbering existing hooks (merge test on 3 fixture settings files). Uninstall restores the original exactly.
  2. The hook returns in < 200 ms and only enqueues (timed test).
  3. The fixture transcript tests/fixtures/sessions/mcp_build.jsonl produces ≥ 1 card that has s ∋ mcp-server-development, d ≥ 3, no metric invented (r == null, needs_metric set), and passes the redaction test (fixture contains a fake AWS key and a client name, and neither appears in the output).
  4. A repo with an existing .git/hooks/post-commit (and a husky repo) still runs its own hook after the global dispatcher is installed.
  5. Adding torch to a watched requirements.txt yields one queued signal after the debounce. Editing a file under an ignore glob yields none.
  6. No recursion: an extraction run produces zero new queue jobs.
  7. (manual) A real 30-min Claude Code session yields a sensible card with no user action, and the background service survives a reboot.

docs.title: 🔁 M3: Multi-device sync ✅
docs.text:
Done 2026-11-27. Five adapters (local, gdrive, usb, syncthing, git) pass one shared conformance suite. The two-spoke/two-adapter headline test passes. USB flush on mount is wired into the agent; criterion 6 (real hardware) is manual.

Scope: Outbox cursors, adapters local, git, gdrive, usb; hub merge, quarantine, registry rebuild and publish; hub.json epochs; cvprism sync, cvprism hub merge|promote|rebuild; suppress, purge.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Headline: two simulated spokes (A via git, B via gdrive folder) plus one card captured on both, merged on the hub, give cards.jsonl with every card exactly once. Both spokes then receive the new registry.
  2. Each adapter passes the shared conformance suite (invariants I1–I5 in SYNC.md), including S2–S5, S8, S9 and S12.
  3. A spoke offline for N ticks pushes the entire backlog on reconnect (property test).
  4. Truncated last lines and conflict-copy files are handled with no loss and no duplicates.
  5. cvprism hub rebuild from inboxes alone reproduces cards.jsonl byte-for-byte (after sorting).
  6. USB mount detection triggers a flush within 15 s on each OS. (manual)

docs.title: 🧾 M4: Compile ✅
docs.text:
Done 2026-11-27. The deterministic honesty gate, citation trace (evidence.md), rejected.md, RenderCV PDF with page-limit fitting, python-docx DOCX, Markdown, BibTeX and ORCID import, and five starter roles are all covered by tests. A real build with Claude ran in about 18 s and produced a 1-page CV.

Scope: Role profiles plus starter roles (academic, industry-ds, applied-ai, hydrodynamics, geospatial), scoring, claude -p drafting, honesty gate, RenderCV PDF, Pandoc DOCX/MD, evidence.md trace, BibTeX/ORCID import.

Acceptance criteria

  1. cvprism build --role applied-ai on the fixture vault produces PDF, DOCX and MD within the page limit.
  2. Every bullet in the output cites ≥ 1 existing card ID in evidence.md.
  3. Injected test: if the LLM stub returns a bullet with a number absent from the cited cards, the gate rejects it and the build reports it.
  4. The LLM input never exceeds limits.cards_to_llm cards (asserted).
  5. Publications render from a .bib file, with the user's name highlighted.
  6. Confidential projects show only display names.

docs.title: 📈 M5: Market intel and JD tailoring ✅
docs.text:
Done 2026-11-27. cvprism build --jd <file|url> with gaps.md; cvprism market add|extract with a hash-keyed LLM cache, so re-runs are deterministic. Market phrases feed role vocabulary automatically. Postings are user-supplied, with no scraping (Open question 7 default).

Scope: cvprism build --jd <file|url>, ad-hoc role from JD, vault/market/<role>.json phrase extraction from user-supplied postings, gap report ("JD asks for X; you have no evidence").

Acceptance criteria

  1. For a fixture JD, the generated CV's skills section covers ≥ 80 % of the JD skills that exist in the registry, and adds none that do not exist.
  2. The gap report lists the JD skills with no evidence.
  3. Market phrase extraction from 20 fixture postings is deterministic given cached LLM output.

docs.title: 🚀 M6: Polish and v1.0 ✅
docs.text:
Done 2026-11-27: browser wizard (init --web), import-linkedin / import-cv, cvprism demo, MkDocs site with Pages deploy, generated CLI reference, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, tag-triggered PyPI and GitHub release workflow, version 1.0.0. Syncthing-daemon CI and age encryption deferred (ADR-014).

Scope: Syncthing adapter, browser-based wizard, optional age encryption, docs site (MkDocs Material), PyPI release, cvprism import (LinkedIn export, existing CV via markitdown), demo vault, contribution guides for roles, adapters and templates.

Acceptance criteria

  1. The Syncthing adapter passes the conformance suite against two real Syncthing instances in CI (containers).
  2. pipx install cvprism and start.sh both work. The 5-minute quick start is timed by a fresh user. (manual)
  3. Docs site published. Every CLI command documented with an example.

docs.title: cvprism File Formats
docs.text:
Status: Phase 0 draft. Schema version v: 1 everywhere. JSON Schema dialect: draft 2020-12. At M1 the schemas below move verbatim into cvprism/schemas/*.schema.json, and this file then links to them.

Artifact Format Owner Location Evidence card JSONL, one card per line Capturing device ~/.cvprism/outbox/<dev>/YYYY-MM.jsonl → vault/inbox/<dev>/YYYY-MM.jsonl → vault/cards.jsonl Skill registry JSON Hub vault/registry.json (spokes cache it as ~/.cvprism/registry.cache.json) Device config YAML Each device ~/.cvprism/device.yaml Profile YAML (+ BibTeX) User vault/profile.yaml Role profile YAML User vault/roles/<role>.yaml (starters in repo roles/) Vault and hub identity JSON Hub vault/vault.json, vault/hub.json (see SYNC.md)

docs.title: 📐 Conventions
docs.text:
• Slugs match ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$, e.g. mcp-server-development, hec-ras.
  • Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC with a Z suffix, second precision.
  • Device IDs are <name-slug>-<4 hex>, e.g. office-01-7f3a. The random suffix prevents two devices called "laptop" from colliding.
  • Compact keys are used only in high-volume JSONL (cards). YAML files people edit use full words (ADR-003).
  • Unknown keys are allowed on read (additionalProperties: true for forward compatibility) and never written by v1 code, except under an x_ prefix for user extensions.

docs.title: 🃏 Evidence card
docs.text: One immutable fact about the user's capability. Cards are never edited. A correction is a new card with sup: [<old id>] (supersedes).

docs.title: Key reference
docs.text: Key Meaning In ID hash? v Schema version (1) no id c_ + first 16 hex chars of sha256 over the canonical form — k Kind, derived from content only: work (non-code achievement: paper, talk, field campaign, award), else result (has r or needs_metric), else skill yes why Novelty reason at capture: new_skill, depth_up, new_result, work, manual (depends on device state, so never hashed) no s Skill slugs, 1–5, sorted yes d Depth level 1–5 (see ADR-011) yes r Result {m, val, unit, base?, dir} or null yes (normalised) ctx Project alias slug (mapped to display text in profile.yaml) or null yes txt Market-facing one-line statement, ≤ 220 chars no meth Methods and techniques, short phrases no tl Tools, libraries, services (slugs) no dom Domain tags (applied-ai, hydrodynamics, geospatial, academic, …) no t Capture time (UTC) no dev Device ID no src claude_session · git_commit · watcher · manual · import no ref Opaque evidence pointer, e.g. git:<repo-alias>@a1b2c3d, cc:<session-hash> no conf Extractor confidence 0–1 (manual = 1) no flags needs_metric, needs_review, low_confidence, manual_raw no sup IDs this card supersedes no lnk Public proof URLs (https, max 5); see Verifiable CVs no lang BCP-47, default en no

docs.title: Canonical form for id
docs.text:
canon = JSON(sort_keys, no whitespace, UTF-8) of
  { "k": k,
    "s": sorted(unique(s)),
    "d": d,
    "r": null | { "m": slug(m), "val": normnum(val), "unit": lower(unit), "dir": dir },
    "ctx": ctx }
id = "c_" + sha256(canon).hex()[:16]

normnum renders a number with no trailing zeros (0.50 → 0.5, 1e3 → 1000). Free text (txt, meth) is excluded on purpose, because LLM wording varies between captures (ADR-002).

docs.title: JSON Schema
docs.text:
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://cvprism.dev/schemas/card.v1.json",
  "title": "cvprism evidence card v1",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["v", "id", "k", "s", "d", "r", "ctx", "txt", "t", "dev", "src"],
  "properties": {
    "v":    { "const": 1 },
    "id":   { "type": "string", "pattern": "^c_[0-9a-f]{16}$" },
    "k":    { "enum": ["skill", "result", "work"] },
    "why":  { "enum": ["new_skill", "depth_up", "new_result", "work", "manual"] },
    "s":    { "type": "array", "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 5, "uniqueItems": true,
              "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/slug" } },
    "d":    { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 5 },
    "r":    { "oneOf": [ { "type": "null" }, { "$ref": "#/$defs/result" } ] },
    "ctx":  { "oneOf": [ { "type": "null" }, { "$ref": "#/$defs/slug" } ] },
    "txt":  { "type": "string", "minLength": 8, "maxLength": 220 },
    "meth": { "type": "array", "maxItems": 8, "items": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 80 } },
    "tl":   { "type": "array", "maxItems": 12, "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/slug" } },
    "dom":  { "type": "array", "maxItems": 6, "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/slug" } },
    "t":    { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
    "dev":  { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*-[0-9a-f]{4}$" },
    "src":  { "enum": ["claude_session", "git_commit", "watcher", "manual", "import"] },
    "ref":  { "type": "string", "maxLength": 120 },
    "conf": { "type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1 },
    "flags":{ "type": "array", "uniqueItems": true,
              "items": { "enum": ["needs_metric", "needs_review", "low_confidence", "manual_raw"] } },
    "sup":  { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^c_[0-9a-f]{16}$" } },
    "lang": { "type": "string", "default": "en" }
  },
  "allOf": [
    { "if": { "properties": { "k": { "const": "result" } } },
      "then": { "anyOf": [
        { "properties": { "r": { "$ref": "#/$defs/result" } } },
        { "properties": { "flags": { "contains": { "const": "needs_metric" } } } }
      ] } }
  ],
  "$defs": {
    "slug": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$", "maxLength": 64 },
    "result": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["m", "val", "unit", "dir"],
      "properties": {
        "m":    { "type": "string", "maxLength": 60, "description": "metric name, e.g. 'inference latency'" },
        "val":  { "type": "number" },
        "unit": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 20, "description": "'%', 'ms', 'x', 'km2', 'users', ..." },
        "base": { "type": ["number", "null"], "description": "baseline value if stated" },
        "dir":  { "enum": ["up", "down", "abs"], "description": "improvement direction or absolute figure" }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: cvprism Security and Privacy
docs.text:
Status: Phase 0 draft. These are design commitments. Each "MUST" becomes a test at M1–M3.

cvprism watches people at work. It is useful only if users trust it with that. The design principle: capture claims about capability, never the work itself.

docs.title: 🚦 Captured vs never captured
docs.text: Captured (in cards) Never captured Skill and tool names (pytorch, hec-ras, mcp-server-development) File contents, source code, notebooks' cells or outputs Methods in market language ("Bayesian calibration of roughness coefficients") Raw data, datasets, model weights, query results Depth level (used → built → published) Client, employer or colleague names, unless the user maps them via profile.yaml projects[].display Measurable results the user or session stated, with units Credentials, tokens, keys, URLs with query strings, hostnames, IPs A project alias slug (ctx) Full transcripts, prompts or diffs (never stored, never copied) Opaque references (git:<repo-alias>@<short-sha>, hashed session ID) Absolute file paths, usernames, repo remote URLs

    accDescr: Raw signals stay on the device. A code-only reducer produces a minimal digest, which is the only thing sent to Claude. The returned candidate is redacted and validated before it becomes a card, and only cards leave the device.

    subgraph device["🔒 Device only"]
        raw_r["Raw signals<br/>transcript · commit · manifest diff"]
        reduce_d["✂️ Reducer (code)<br/>allow-list extraction"]
        digest_d["Digest ≤ 6k tokens"]
        redact_x["🛡️ Redactor + secret scan"]
        card_c["Card"]
    end
    llm_l["🤖 claude -p<br/>(user's own account)"]
    transport_t["Transports"]

    raw_r --> reduce_d --> digest_d --> llm_l --> redact_x --> card_c --> transport_t

    classDef safe fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px,color:#14532d
    classDef ext fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#ca8a04,stroke-width:2px,color:#713f12
    class reduce_d,redact_x safe
    class llm_l,transport_t ext
  1. Reducer (code, allow-list). It keeps only fields on an allow-list:
  2. Claude session: user prompts truncated to 300 chars each, tool names and counts, file extensions touched, package names seen in install commands, the final assistant summary (truncated).
  3. git: commit subject, changed file extensions and counts, changed dependency names in manifests. No diff hunks.
  4. Watcher: added or removed dependency names, new SKILL.md/.mcp.json server names, notebook kernel language.
  5. Before anything leaves the reducer, the redaction rules below are applied to the digest itself.
  6. LLM call. The digest goes to claude -p under whatever account is logged in on that device. That is the same provider that already saw the session, but possibly a different account. Users who need stricter handling set capture.claude_session.enabled: false, or use review_mode, or exclude paths.
  7. Redactor (after LLM). Runs on every candidate card field.
  8. Validation. A JSON Schema check that also enforces length caps, so no field can carry a paste of content.

docs.title: ✂️ Redaction hooks
docs.text:
~/.cvprism/redact.yaml, per device, never synced (it may itself contain sensitive names):

v: 1
deny_terms:            # case-insensitive, whole-word; matched card -> term replaced, card flagged needs_review
  - "Contoso"
  - "Project Nightingale"
replace:               # literal or regex -> replacement
  - {pattern: "(?i)acme water", with: "a water utility"}
exclude_paths:         # signals from these paths are dropped before the reducer
  - "~/Documents/clients/**"
secret_scanners: [aws, gcp, github, openai, anthropic, private_key, jwt, high_entropy]
on_secret: drop        # drop | quarantine
plugins: []            # dotted paths to callables: (card: dict) -> dict | None
  • Secret scanning uses built-in regexes for common key formats, plus a Shannon-entropy check on tokens ≥ 20 chars. A card that hits is dropped by default and never reaches the outbox.
  • Plugins let organisations add their own rules (e.g. a client-list lookup) as one Python callable. Returning None drops the card.
  • Review mode (privacy.review_mode: true) writes cards to ~/.cvprism/pending/. cvprism review shows each one for approve, edit or drop before it enters the outbox.

docs.title: Removing data
docs.text:
Append-only applies to normal operation. For real mistakes (e.g. a secret slipped through):

  • cvprism suppress <id> hides a card from merge and compile. The history is kept.
  • cvprism purge <id> is the one deliberate exception to append-only. It rewrites the affected inbox month file on the local outbox and on every reachable transport, rewrites cards.jsonl on the hub, and records the ID in vault/purged.txt, so lagging transports are filtered at merge. For git it also prints the history-rewrite commands (git filter-repo) for the user to run. cvprism never force-pushes on its own.

docs.title: cvprism Sync Protocol
docs.text: Status: Phase 0 draft. Decisions: ADR-001, ADR-004, ADR-005, ADR-006, ADR-012.

docs.title: 🧷 Invariants
docs.text:
The protocol is safe over every transport because of five invariants. Every adapter MUST preserve them, and the test suite checks them for each adapter.

# Invariant Consequence I1 A device writes only to inbox/<own-device-id>/ on a transport Two writers never touch the same path, so there are no write conflicts I2 Inbox files are append-only. Each record is one complete line ending in \n Remote state is always a prefix (or equal) of local state, and a truncated last line is detectable I3 Card IDs are content hashes (ADR-002) Merging is set union. Duplicates via two routes are harmless I4 Only the hub of the highest epoch writes registry.json, cards.jsonl, hub.json Hub-owned files have one writer I5 Every transport root holds vault.json with vault_id, checked before any read or write Vaults never mix

Because merge is a union of immutable, content-addressed records, the system is a grow-only set CRDT. Delivery order, duplication and delay do not affect the final state.

docs.title: 🗂️ Transport layout
docs.text:
Every adapter exposes the same logical tree at its transport root:

<transport-root>/
├── vault.json                # {"v":1,"vault_id":"…","created":"…"}
├── hub.json                  # {"v":1,"hub_device_id":"home-pc-9a0b","epoch":1}   (hub-owned)
├── registry.json             # hub-owned, see SCHEMA.md
└── inbox/
    ├── office-01-7f3a/
    │   ├── 2026-10.jsonl
    │   └── 2026-11.jsonl
    └── lab-ws-3c1d/
        └── 2026-11.jsonl

On the hub, vault/ is a superset of this tree. It adds cards.jsonl, profile.yaml, roles/, market/, quarantine/ and build/. For the git adapter the transport is a git repo of this tree. If you want the whole vault versioned, point the hub's vault at the same repo (Open question 8).

docs.title: 🔌 Adapter interface
docs.text:
class Adapter(Protocol):
    name: str
    def available(self) -> bool: ...                        # cheap probe, no side effects
    def push(self, outbox: Outbox) -> PushReport: ...       # spoke + hub: replicate own inbox files
    def pull(self) -> Registry | None: ...                  # spoke: newest registry visible at transport
    def status(self) -> AdapterStatus: ...                  # last push/pull, backlog bytes, errors
    # hub-only extensions
    def pull_inboxes(self, dest: Path) -> PullReport: ...   # copy all inbox/<dev>/*.jsonl to staging
    def publish(self, files: dict[str, Path]) -> None: ...  # write hub-owned files

docs.title: Push algorithm (all adapters)
docs.text:
for file in outbox/<dev>/*.jsonl:
    local = (size, sha256)
    if cursor[adapter][file] == local: continue          # nothing new
    write remote tmp file  inbox/<dev>/.<file>.tmp       # full copy; files are small (KB–MB)
    atomic rename → inbox/<dev>/<file>                   # or adapter-native commit
    cursor[adapter][file] = local

Whole-file copy with an atomic rename is used instead of a remote append. It is idempotent, needs no remote locking, and synced-folder clients handle it better than in-place appends. A month file rarely exceeds 1 MB (about 2,000 cards).

docs.title: Hub pull and merge
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    accTitle: Hub Merge Algorithm
    accDescr: The hub pulls inbox files from each adapter into staging, parses complete lines only, validates each card, quarantines invalid ones, unions valid cards by ID into cards.jsonl, then rebuilds and publishes the registry if anything changed.

    start_s(["Merge tick or manual cvprism hub merge"])
    pull_p["For each available adapter:<br/>pull_inboxes → staging/<adapter>/"]
    glob_g["Glob staging/*/inbox/*/*.jsonl<br/>(includes conflict copies)"]
    parse_p["Parse lines ending in \n<br/>ignore unterminated tail"]
    valid_v{"Schema valid,<br/>id recomputes,<br/>vault matches?"}
    quar_q[("quarantine/<dev>.jsonl")]
    union_u["Union by id into cards.jsonl<br/>(keep earliest t; append new only)"]
    changed_c{"New cards?"}
    reg_r["Rebuild registry.json<br/>rev+1"]
    pub_p["publish(registry.json, hub.json)<br/>to every adapter"]
    done_d(["Done"])

    start_s --> pull_p --> glob_g --> parse_p --> valid_v
    valid_v -->|"no"| quar_q
    valid_v -->|"yes"| union_u --> changed_c
    changed_c -->|"yes"| reg_r --> pub_p --> done_d
    changed_c -->|"no"| done_d

    classDef store fill:#f3e8ff,stroke:#7c3aed,stroke-width:2px,color:#3b0764
    class quar_q store

Cards that are valid but not novel against the hub's state at merge time are kept with an extra x_late: true field (ADR-011). Push never shrinks a remote file: it writes the union of remote and local lines minus purged IDs, so a restored or reinstalled device cannot erase history.

The hub recomputes each id from the canonical fields. A mismatch means corruption or tampering, and the line is quarantined. cards.jsonl is append-only on the hub too, and can always be rebuilt from scratch with cvprism hub rebuild from all inboxes.

docs.title: Multiple adapters at once
docs.text:
A device pushes to every available adapter on each tick (default every 15 min, plus on-demand). Each adapter keeps its own cursor, so a card reaches the hub by whichever route arrives first. Later arrivals by other routes dedup by ID. The hub pulls from every adapter it has configured.

A spoke accepts the registry with the highest (epoch, rev) across all adapters, so a USB stick carrying an old registry cannot roll a spoke back.

docs.title: 📴 Offline and conflict scenarios
docs.text: Scenario What happens Final state S1. Spoke offline for 3 weeks Cards append to the local outbox. status shows the backlog. On reconnect, every changed month file is pushed Complete. No loss, no duplicates S2. Same card sent via git and USB The hub sees it twice and the union keeps one One card S3. Drive creates 2026-11 (1).jsonl The hub globs both. Lines in both dedup by ID Complete S4. USB yanked mid-write The tmp file is left. The rename never happened, so the old full file is intact. Next mount: tmp is overwritten Complete S5. Drive uploads a half-written file The hub ignores the unterminated last line and picks it up next merge Complete, delayed S6. Spoke clock wrong by +1 year Its cards land in a future month file. Ordering cosmetics only Complete. doctor warns on skew > 1 day vs git/Drive timestamps S7. Hub laptop dies cvprism hub promote on another device. With epoch+1 it rebuilds cards.jsonl from all inboxes on all transports Complete, except the dead hub's own unsynced cards S8. Old hub comes back Reads hub.json with a higher epoch, demotes itself to spoke, pushes its inbox Complete S9. Two hubs promoted concurrently (same epoch) Tie broken by lexicographically higher hub_device_id. The loser demotes on next tick Converges S10. Spoke has never seen a registry Novelty filter runs against an empty registry, so every candidate becomes a card. The hub dedups and re-checks novelty at merge (a stale card is kept but flagged needs_review if not novel) Some extra cards, all correct S11b. A device purges its own card cvprism purge <id> rewrites its outbox and its inbox on every reachable transport, and appends the ID to inbox/<dev>/purged.txt. The hub unions all purged.txt into vault/purged.txt and removes the card from cards.jsonl and its inbox copies Card erased everywhere the device and the hub can reach; git history needs a manual git filter-repo S11. User wants a card gone Inboxes stay append-only. cvprism suppress <id> adds the ID to hub-owned vault/suppressed.txt (one per line), which the merge and the compiler honour. A correction is a new card with sup: [<id>] Card hidden from CVs, history kept S12. Wrong vault's USB stick plugged in vault_id mismatch. The adapter refuses and logs No change

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev,all]"      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\pip
.venv/bin/python -m pytest

Rules of the house:

  • Tests first. Every behaviour change starts with a failing test.
  • Never commit personal data. *.jsonl outside tests/fixtures/ is git-ignored for a reason. Fixtures use synthetic people only.
  • Privacy boundary. Capture code may keep names, counts and the user's own words, never file contents, tool output, diffs or data (see docs/SECURITY_PRIVACY.md).
  • Honesty gate. Nothing may add a claim or number to a CV that the evidence doesn't support.
  • Cross-platform. CI runs Windows, macOS and Linux on Python 3.10 and 3.13.
  • Report security issues privately (SECURITY.md); see also the code of conduct.
  • Regenerate the CLI reference when you change commands: typer cvprism.cli utils docs --name cvprism --title "CLI reference" --output docs/guide/cli.md.

docs.title: Commit and PR style
docs.text: Conventional-style subjects (feat(sync): ..., fix(compile): ...). One logical change per commit. PRs describe what changed, why, and how it was tested.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text:
Each ADR records one non-obvious choice: its context, the decision, the alternatives and the consequences. ADRs are immutable once Accepted. To change a decision, write a new ADR that supersedes it.

ADR Title Status 001 Hub-and-spoke topology with append-only per-device inboxes Proposed 002 Card IDs hash canonical fields, not free text Proposed (amends kickoff spec) 003 Plain files; compact-key JSONL for cards only Proposed 004 Local outbox is the source of truth; spokes hold no vault Proposed (amends kickoff spec) 005 Adapter interface and whole-file atomic replication Proposed 006 Syncthing instead of a custom LAN server Proposed 007 Hooks only enqueue; extraction via headless claude -p over a code-reduced digest Proposed (amends kickoff spec) 008 Global git hooks path with a chaining dispatcher Proposed (amends kickoff spec) 009 Deterministic honesty gate for CV bullets Proposed 010 RenderCV for PDF, Pandoc for DOCX/MD Proposed (amends kickoff spec) 011 Five-level depth ladder and novelty rules Proposed 012 Hub identity and promotion via epochs Proposed 013 Venv in the user data dir; OS-native login services Proposed 014 What v1.0 deliberately leaves out Accepted 015 Verifiable CV through project-level visibility and computed proof levels Accepted 016 Recruiter-ready output: code-enforced writing rules and an ATS read-back Accepted 017 Signed builds with existing SSH keys, and an open manifest specification Accepted 018 A local, server-rendered browser app for non-developers Accepted

Template: Context → Decision → Alternatives considered → Consequences.

docs.title: ADR-001: Hub-and-spoke topology with append-only per-device inboxes
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Users work on several machines, possibly under different Claude accounts, and want one place to build CVs. The transports we must support (git, consumer synced folders, USB sticks, Syncthing) have very different consistency semantics. Synced folders in particular produce conflict copies and partial uploads.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• One hub per vault. All other devices are spokes. Spokes never talk to each other.
  • Each device writes only to inbox/<device-id>/YYYY-MM.jsonl, append-only, one complete line per record.
  • The hub is the single writer of cards.jsonl and registry.json.
  • Merge is a set union by content-hash ID (ADR-002). The data model is a grow-only set CRDT.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Option Why not Single shared cards.jsonl written by all devices Concurrent writes conflict on every transport, git included Peer-to-peer mesh (every device merges) N² sync paths, harder reasoning. CVs are built on one machine anyway SQLite per device and a replication tool Binary files sync badly over Drive and USB, and break the "plain files" requirement

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Conflict-free on every transport by construction. Correctness does not depend on clocks or delivery order.
  • Files grow forever. At around 2 KB/card and a few cards a day this is about 1 MB/year, which is acceptable.
  • Deletion needs explicit mechanisms (suppress, purge; see SECURITY_PRIVACY.md).
  • The hub is a soft single point of failure for compiling, mitigated by ADR-012 (promotion and rebuild from inboxes).

docs.title: ADR-002: Card IDs hash canonical fields, not free text
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed. This amends the kickoff spec, which said "sha256 of normalised fields, excluding device and timestamp".
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The kickoff spec wants the same achievement captured twice anywhere to dedup automatically. But the two captures come from an LLM, often from different sources (a Claude session and a git commit). Their wording (txt, meth) will almost never match byte-for-byte. A hash that includes free text would dedup almost nothing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
id = "c_" + sha256(canonical_json({k, sorted(s), d, normalised r, ctx}))[:16]

  • Only structured fields are hashed: kind, skill slugs (after registry alias normalisation), depth, normalised result, and project alias.
  • Free text, tools, domains, confidence, device, timestamp and source are excluded.
  • The ID is truncated to 64 bits. The birthday bound for collisions is about 4×10⁹ cards, far beyond a personal vault. The hub recomputes IDs on merge.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Option Why not Hash all fields except device/time Near-zero dedup across sources, as above Embedding-similarity dedup Non-deterministic, needs a model on every device. May be added later as an advisory hub-side pass UUIDs plus a hub-side LLM dedup Costs tokens on every merge, non-reproducible

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Dedup quality depends on slug normalisation. The registry alias table is therefore on the critical path, and the extractor must choose slugs from the registry when one fits (it gets the top-N candidate slugs in its prompt).
  • Two genuinely different achievements with identical structure (e.g. two different MCP servers at depth 3 with no ctx) collapse into one card. That is acceptable: for novelty they are the same evidence, and ctx separates them when it matters.
  • k must be a pure function of card content (work > result > skill). An earlier draft had a depth kind, but whether something is a level-up depends on what the capturing device already knows. That would give the same achievement different IDs on different devices, so the novelty reason now lives in the unhashed why field.
  • Changing the canonical form is a breaking change and needs v: 2 plus a migration.

docs.title: ADR-003: Plain files; compact-key JSONL for cards only
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Requirements: no database, user-readable data, low token cost, line-oriented append for sync safety.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Cards: JSONL with short keys (k, s, d, r, txt, …). One card per line. UTF-8, \n line endings on every OS.
  • Registry: pretty-printed JSON (hub-generated, diff-friendly).
  • Everything a human edits (profile.yaml, roles/*.yaml, device.yaml, redact.yaml): YAML with full-word keys, loaded with ruamel.yaml so comments survive round-trips.
  • JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) is the single source of truth for all formats.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: SQLite (binary, sync-hostile); one Markdown file per card (thousands of files, slow on Drive and USB, awkward to validate); CSV (no nesting for results).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Compact keys cut card size by about 35 % and reduce LLM tokens when cards go to the compiler. They are less readable, so cvprism show pretty-prints with full names and SCHEMA.md documents every key.

docs.title: ADR-004: Local outbox is the source of truth; spokes hold no vault
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed. This amends the kickoff layout, which implied every device writes into a vault/inbox/<device-id>/ folder.
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: If a spoke's only copy of a card lives inside a transport folder (a Drive folder, a git clone, a USB stick), then removing the stick or a Drive "free up space" action can lose it. A spoke that holds a full vault also means a lost laptop exposes the whole career history and profile.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Every device writes cards first to ~/.cvprism/outbox/<device-id>/YYYY-MM.jsonl on local disk.
  • Adapters replicate outbox files to inbox/<device-id>/ at each transport, tracking a (size, sha256) cursor per adapter and file.
  • Spokes receive only registry.json, hub.json and vault.json. Only the hub holds cards.jsonl and profile.yaml.
  • The hub's own captures use the local adapter into its own vault, so the code path is the same.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The offline outbox comes for free: it is the outbox.
  • Multiple adapters are independent. Each has its own cursor.
  • Building a CV away from the hub is not possible in v1 (Open question 8 in ARCHITECTURE.md).

docs.title: ADR-005: Adapter interface and whole-file atomic replication
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Adding a transport should take one Python module. Transports differ: git has commits, synced folders have eventual consistency and conflict copies, USB has mount events.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Interface: available(), push(outbox), pull() -> Registry | None, status(). Hub extensions: pull_inboxes(dest), publish(files).
  • push copies whole changed files via write-to-tmp then atomic rename (or a commit for git). It never appends in place remotely.
  • Adapters are discovered via Python entry points (cvprism.adapters), so third parties can ship adapters as separate packages.
  • A shared conformance test suite (tests/conformance/) runs against every adapter.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Remote append with byte offsets (fragile on synced folders, which may upload a stale whole file); rsync (not available on Windows by default); per-card files (file-count explosion).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Simple and idempotent. Re-copying a month file costs bandwidth proportional to its size (about 1 MB at most), which is negligible.

docs.title: ADR-006: Syncthing instead of a custom LAN server
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The user wants machines on the same LAN to sync with no cloud. A homemade server must handle discovery, NAT and firewalls, TLS, auth, resumable transfer and Windows service quirks. That is months of edge cases outside our core value.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Ship a syncthing adapter that treats a Syncthing-shared folder like a plain folder. cvprism generates the folder configuration and pairing instructions, and checks Syncthing's local REST API for health. A native cvprism hub serve stays on the post-v1 roadmap.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The user installs Syncthing (open source, cross-platform). Both machines must be online at the same time for transfer, and the outbox covers the gaps. Transport security and resumption come from a mature project.

docs.title: ADR-007: Hooks only enqueue; extraction via headless claude -p over a code-reduced digest
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed. This amends the kickoff spec, which had the SessionEnd hook run the extraction.
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• A SessionEnd hook that runs a multi-second LLM call blocks or slows session shutdown, and may be killed.
  • claude -p is itself a Claude Code session. Its own SessionEnd would trigger the hook again, causing recursion.
  • Full transcripts are large (tokens = cost) and contain file contents and data (privacy).
  • The user may use different Claude accounts per device. cvprism must not depend on account state.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Hooks (Claude Code, git, watcher) append a small job record to ~/.cvprism/queue/ and exit. Target < 200 ms.
  2. The background worker drains the queue. It sets CVPRISM_EXTRACTING=1, and the hook is a no-op when that variable is present.
  3. A code-only reducer builds an allow-listed digest (see SECURITY_PRIVACY.md), capped at max_input_tokens.
  4. The extractor calls claude -p --output-format json with all tools disabled, an optional --model (a cheap model by default), and a JSON Schema in the prompt. The output is validated, with one retry and then rejection.
  5. An internal LLM-backend interface is kept, so a direct API or local-model backend can be added later without touching capture.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Works with whatever account is logged in. No API key handling in cvprism.
  • Capture has a delay of minutes, which is fine for CVs.
  • If claude is unavailable, jobs wait (TTL 30 days) and manual --raw logging still works.
  • Exact CLI flags (tool disabling, model selection, hook payload fields) are pinned and covered by tests at M2, because they can change between Claude Code releases.

docs.title: ADR-008: Global git hooks path with a chaining dispatcher
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed. This amends the kickoff spec ("git post-commit hook (global hooks path)").
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Setting git config --global core.hooksPath makes git ignore every repository's own .git/hooks/. It also replaces any hooks path the user already set globally. Users of pre-commit, husky or lefthook would silently lose their hooks, which would kill adoption. Repos that set a local core.hooksPath (husky does) override the global one, so cvprism would never see their commits.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Install a dispatcher directory ~/.cvprism/git-hooks/ containing a script for every client-side hook name. Each script:
  • runs cvprism's handler (for post-commit only),
  • then runs the repo-local $GIT_DIR/hooks/<name> if present and executable,
  • then runs the previous global hooks path's <name> if one was set before install,
  • and propagates exit codes for blocking hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push).
  • Record the previous core.hooksPath in device.yaml and restore it exactly on uninstall.
  • For repos with a local core.hooksPath, cvprism doctor lists them and offers an opt-in per-repo shim.
  • cvprism's own handler never blocks a commit: it enqueues and always exits 0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Existing tooling keeps working. Repos using husky and similar need a one-time opt-in, which is documented.

docs.title: ADR-009: Deterministic honesty gate for CV bullets
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: "Never invent metrics" cannot be guaranteed by prompting alone. LLMs embellish, especially when tailoring to a job description.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The compiler asks the LLM for bullets in a structured form {text, cites: [card ids]}, then applies a code gate:

  1. cites is non-empty, and every ID exists in cards.jsonl and is not suppressed.
  2. Every numeric token in text (digits, %, x/×, ranges, number words such as "two" to "twenty", "dozens", "hundreds") must match a value in a cited card's r (val, base, or a derived delta/ratio within ±1 % rounding) or a profile.yaml facts entry.
  3. Skill names in the bullet should map to slugs in the cited cards or their registry parents. This is a soft check that warns rather than rejects.
  4. A failing bullet gets one repair attempt with the failure reason. Then it is dropped and listed in build/…/rejected.md.

Every build also writes evidence.md, which maps each bullet to its cards.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Some legitimate phrasing is rejected (e.g. "two-phase approach" triggers on "two"). We accept these false positives and refine with an allow-list of non-metric number phrases. Users can always add a facts entry to assert a number themselves.

docs.title: ADR-010: RenderCV for PDF, Pandoc for DOCX/MD
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed. This amends "LaTeX→PDF" in the kickoff spec, pending verification at M4.
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: We must not build a typesetter. RenderCV takes a YAML CV model and renders a PDF with several maintained themes. Recent major versions moved from LaTeX to Typst as the engine, which installs via pip as a small dependency. A full TeX distribution is around 1–4 GB, which conflicts with plug-and-play install from a USB stick. DOCX is still required by many recruiters and ATS portals.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The compiler emits a RenderCV-compatible YAML model, and RenderCV produces the PDF with whatever engine the pinned version uses (Typst expected).
  • The compiler emits a Markdown CV. Pandoc (an external binary, optional dependency) converts it to DOCX using a reference .docx in templates/.
  • LaTeX source output (tex) is offered only if the pinned RenderCV version supports it. Not a v1 requirement.
  • Pin the RenderCV version and isolate it behind compile/render/rendercv.py, so it can be swapped.

docs.title: Verified at M4 (2026-11-27)
docs.text:
• RenderCV 2.8 renders via Typst (no TeX install), 9 themes: classic, ember, engineeringclassic, engineeringresumes, harvard, ink, moderncv, opal, sb2nov. Pinned as rendercv[full]>=2.8,<3. It needs Python ≥ 3.12, so PDF output is an optional extra (pip install cvprism[pdf]).
  • A bare year must be passed as an integer (a string "2023" renders as "Jan 2023").
  • Page count comes from RenderCV's per-page PNG export, so no PDF library is needed. When a CV exceeds the role's page limit, the build drops bullets per position until it fits.
  • DOCX: python-docx instead of Pandoc. Pandoc is an external binary that most users lack (it was missing on the reference machine). python-docx is pip-installable and writes ATS-friendly DOCX directly from the CV model. Pandoc is no longer needed.

docs.title: Original verification checklist
docs.text: The exact RenderCV version, its YAML schema, its engine (Typst or LaTeX) and its theme list. Re-confirm the licences of RenderCV and Pandoc against our Apache-2.0 licence (Pandoc is invoked as a separate process, not linked).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Install stays small. DOCX styling is limited to what a Pandoc reference document can express, which is acceptable for ATS-friendly output.

docs.title: ADR-011: Five-level depth ladder and novelty rules
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The novelty filter must tell "used an API" from "built an MCP server" in a way that is deterministic once the extractor has assigned a level.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
d Level Typical evidence 1 Used Called an API, ran a tool, followed a tutorial 2 Applied Used it to deliver part of a real project 3 Built Built or integrated a component or system with it (e.g. an MCP server, a calibrated model) 4 Led / production Deployed to production, optimised with measured results, led others, owned the decision 5 Authored / taught Published, taught, contributed upstream, created a method others use

Novelty rule for a candidate card c against registry R:

emit card if  any(slug not in R for slug in c.s)           # new skill
          or  any(c.d > R[slug].max_d for slug in c.s)     # depth up
          or  (c.r and fp(c.r) not in R[slug].rh)           # new measurable result
          or  c.k == "work"                                 # papers, talks, field work: always
else          counters[slug].n += 1; counters[slug].last = now

The reason that fired is stored in the card's unhashed why field (new_skill, depth_up, new_result, work).

On a device, the known state is the union of the hub registry cache and the device's own outbox. Otherwise a single machine, or a spoke that has not yet seen a registry, would re-emit every card.

The hub re-applies the rule at merge against the authoritative registry. A non-novel card that arrives late is kept (it is valid evidence) but flagged needs_review.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The extractor's rubric must state the ladder explicitly, with examples per level. Depth is a claim: the honesty gate does not verify it, and review mode lets users correct it.

docs.title: ADR-012: Hub identity and promotion via epochs
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: "A device can be promoted to hub later." Without coordination, two hubs could publish competing registries (split brain), especially over slow transports like USB.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• hub.json = {v, hub_device_id, epoch}, written only by the hub.
  • cvprism hub promote reads the highest hub.json across all reachable transports, writes epoch+1 with its own ID, then runs hub rebuild from all inboxes.
  • Every hub checks hub.json before each merge. If it sees a higher epoch (or an equal epoch with a lexicographically greater device ID), it demotes itself to spoke.
  • Registries carry (epoch, rev). Spokes accept only strictly newer ones.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: There is no consensus protocol, and none is needed. The worst case is a temporary second registry. That is harmless, because registries only steer novelty and the hub re-checks at merge.

docs.title: ADR-013: Venv in the user data dir; OS-native login services
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Install must work from a git clone or a USB stick, and capture must continue after the stick is removed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• start.sh / start.bat locate Python ≥ 3.10, create a venv in the platform data dir (%LOCALAPPDATA%\cvprism, ~/Library/Application Support/cvprism, ~/.local/share/cvprism) and pip install cvprism from the stick or clone path. A bundled wheelhouse on the USB stick allows offline install. After install, nothing references the stick.
  • The background service (cvprism agent) is registered per OS: on Windows the per-user HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run registry value launching pythonw -m cvprism agent (no admin rights; an "at logon" scheduled task was the first choice but needs elevation on many machines), a macOS launchd LaunchAgent, or a Linux systemd --user unit with an XDG autostart fallback.
  • Hooks point at the venv's absolute cvprism executable path.
  • cvprism uninstall removes services and hooks, restores prior git and Claude Code settings, and keeps data unless --purge-data is given.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: pipx (good, but not guaranteed to be installed; supported as an alternative path), a PyInstaller single binary (large, and antivirus false positives on Windows), Docker (cannot easily hook the host's Claude Code or git).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: No admin rights needed on any OS. Python must already be installed. The start script prints per-OS install instructions if it is missing.

docs.title: ADR-014: What v1.0 deliberately leaves out
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The M6 roadmap listed Syncthing CI against real instances and optional age encryption of transport files. Both are useful but neither blocks a correct, safe v1.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Syncthing CI with real daemons: deferred. The Syncthing adapter is a plain-folder adapter. It passes the same conformance suite as gdrive/local, and transport correctness belongs to Syncthing itself. Pairing two daemons in CI adds flaky infrastructure for little extra assurance.
  • age encryption of inbox files: deferred to v1.1. Cards contain no secrets by construction (reducer allow-list, redactor, schema length caps). Encryption needs key distribution to every spoke, which deserves its own design.
  • PyPI publishing: automated in release.yml via trusted publishing. The owner enables it once on pypi.org.
  • Native cvprism hub serve: post-v1, as ADR-006 already decided.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: v1 users who need encryption at rest on a shared transport should use an encrypted private git repo or their cloud provider's encryption. SECURITY_PRIVACY.md documents this exposure.

docs.title: ADR-015: Verifiable CV through project-level visibility and computed proof levels
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-28
  • Spec: 2026-11-28 Verifiable CV design

docs.title: Context
docs.text: In 2026 recruiters report they cannot trust CVs, and detection of AI-polished CVs performs no better than chance. cvprism's honesty gate is invisible to a reader. We need checkable proof on the CV itself, without exposing private work and without demoting skills learned in closed-source projects.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Visibility is a property of the project (public | private | local), stored only on the hub. Cards stay immutable and links are resolved at build time.
  2. Proof levels are computed from evidence (public, confirmed, captured, self-reported), never entered by the user.
  3. Private work is first-class. It always appears; only the link is replaced by (private repository), or by nothing for local work.
  4. Verification is self-hosted: an Evidence appendix in every CV, plus an optional static page on the user's own GitHub Pages with a SHA-256 fingerprint of the PDF. There is no central server (consistent with ADR-001/ADR-014).
  5. Links appear as visible URL text, not icons, to keep the CV ATS-safe.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Links stored inside cards: rejected, because visibility changes over time and cards are immutable.
  • Automatic linking of any public-host remote: rejected, because it risks advertising repos the user didn't intend to.
  • A central verify service: deferred. It needs servers and accounts, and could come later as an optional layer.
  • Per-bullet proof symbols: rejected, because they can confuse ATS parsers. Levels live in the appendix instead.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A truthful candidate's CV becomes distinguishable: proof is one click away.
  • A self-hosted fingerprint proves integrity, not truth. The UI says this explicitly.
  • Users must mark projects public once. cvprism project set makes that a single command.

docs.title: ADR-016: Recruiter-ready output through code-enforced writing rules and an ATS read-back
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: An honest CV still has to win the first 10 seconds with a recruiter and survive an ATS parser. The owner asked for CVs that never repeat themselves, never sound boring, and are ready for applicant tracking systems. As with the honesty gate (ADR-009), these are rules we can check in code instead of hoping a prompt follows them.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Writing quality (compile/quality.py)

  • Near-duplicate lines (same skills and ≥ 60 % word overlap) are merged into the stronger line: higher proof level, then score. Their citations are combined.
  • Repeated opening verbs: the second and later uses of a verb are swapped for a vetted synonym from the same meaning group (Built → Developed → Engineered …). This is applied only when the bullet starts with that verb, so meaning is preserved and the honesty gate still passes.
  • Weak openers ("Responsible for", "Worked on", "Helped"), buzzwords ("passionate", "results-driven", "synergy") and over-long lines (> 35 words) are reported in quality.md. With Claude drafting enabled, the prompt forbids them and asks for challenge → action → result lines.

ATS read-back (compile/ats.py)

  • After rendering, cvprism extracts the text of cv.pdf (pypdf) and cv.docx (python-docx) the way a parser would, then checks:
  • the name and email appear near the top
  • standard section headings are present
  • every bullet's text survives extraction
  • proof links are visible as text, not hidden behind icons
  • the file is under 2 MB
  • With --jd, it scores keyword coverage. It reports JD skills that have evidence but didn't make it into the CV (an opportunity) separately from real gaps (no evidence, never added).
  • Results go to ats.md and a one-line summary in the build log.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Asking the LLM to "avoid repetition": not enforceable, and unavailable in --no-llm builds.
  • Paraphrasing whole bullets in code: risks changing meaning, so only the first verb is swapped.
  • Third-party ATS scoring APIs: they would send the CV off-device, so they're rejected.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Two new artifacts per build: quality.md and ats.md. pypdf joins the [pdf] extra. ATS checks are heuristics; they catch real breakages (lost text, hidden contacts, odd headings) but no tool can guarantee every ATS vendor's behaviour.

docs.title: ADR-017: Signed builds with existing SSH keys, and an open manifest specification
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The verify page (ADR-015) proves a CV file wasn't altered, but anyone could publish a page under any name. Recruiters also need a way to check CVs that doesn't depend on cvprism existing, if the format is ever to become an industry habit.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Sign with the key people already have. cvprism build --sign signs manifest.json with ssh-keygen -Y sign (namespace cvprism-cv), using the SSH key the author uses for GitHub. GitHub publishes every user's public keys at github.com/<user>.keys, so cvprism verify --github <user> (or plain OpenSSH) checks who produced the CV. There are no new key types, no accounts, and no servers.
  2. Publish the format as an open spec (docs/spec/evidence-linked-cv-v1.md, Apache-2.0) with a JSON Schema, so other builders and ATS vendors can produce and consume it.
  3. Publish the exact bytes. The verify page copies the build's manifest.json byte-for-byte, so signatures remain valid.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• W3C Verifiable Credentials / Open Badges 3.0: the right long-term home for third-party attestations, but heavy for a self-asserted CV today (DID methods, JSON-LD). The spec leaves room for a future confirmed level backed by VCs.
  • GPG signatures: fewer people have GPG keys than SSH keys on GitHub.
  • A central signing service: needs servers and accounts, which we rejected in ADR-014.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Signing requires OpenSSH ≥ 8.2 (Git for Windows and current macOS/Linux include it). A signature binds the manifest to a key holder; it does not make claims true. The spec and the verify page both say so.

docs.title: ADR-018: A local, server-rendered browser app for non-developers
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-11-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: cvprism's mission needs people who never open a terminal: researchers, field scientists, consultants. The engine is complete; what's missing is a front door.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• cvprism app serves a small web app on 127.0.0.1 using only the standard library (http.server). Double-clicking start.bat/start.sh with no arguments sets up in the browser and opens the app.
  • Server-rendered HTML, no JavaScript. It's fast, accessible, easy to audit, and allows a strict CSP (default-src 'none').
  • Security:
  • a one-time key in the URL becomes an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie
  • every form carries a CSRF token
  • the Host header must be localhost (DNS-rebinding defence)
  • all output is escaped
  • uploads are capped at 25 MB, written to a temporary folder, and type-checked by extension
  • downloads are confined to the vault's build/ folder
  • Same engine: every page calls the same functions as the CLI, so honesty rules can't diverge.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Electron/Tauri desktop app: a large download and a second toolchain, for little gain.
  • A hosted web app: contradicts "your data stays on your computers" (ADR-001, ADR-014).
  • A single-page React app: needs a JS build pipeline and weakens the CSP.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The app must keep running while in use (it says so). Mobile access isn't supported, by design: the server binds to localhost only.

docs.title: The cvprism app (no terminal needed)
docs.text:
Not a developer? You don't need a terminal. Double-click start.bat (Windows) or run start.sh (macOS/Linux). The first time, a setup page opens in your browser. After that, every double-click opens the cvprism app.

You can also open it any time with:

cvprism app

The app runs only on your own computer. It's protected by a one-time key, and nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose a sync transport.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text: Page What it's for Home Your evidence at a glance: how many cards, how many have public proof, your projects, your last CV Add evidence One achievement at a time: what you did, skills, how deep ("I used it" → "I published or taught it"), a result if you measured one, a proof link, the project. Tick "This isn't code" for papers, talks, field work, awards and teaching Bring in what you have Upload your LinkedIn data export (.zip) or an old CV (.docx, .md, .txt, .pdf) Projects Choose how each project appears: Public (blue proof links), Private repository (skills listed, no links) or Local only My evidence Your most recent cards and how strong their proof is Build a CV Pick a role, or paste a job posting. Download the PDF, Word and Markdown files, and read the ATS check, gap report and writing-quality report on the same page

docs.title: Honesty is built in
docs.text:
The app uses the same engine as the command line:

  • A number appears on your CV only if you typed it.
  • Every line points to its evidence.
  • Private work keeps its skills.
  • Claude may polish wording, but it cannot add claims.

docs.title: On your other computers
docs.text: Every computer can add evidence through the app. CVs are built on your main computer (the hub); other computers send their evidence there automatically.

docs.title: Building CVs
docs.text: CVs are built on the hub from your evidence cards plus profile.yaml: the facts cvprism never infers, such as your name, positions, education and publications.

docs.title: For a role
docs.text:
cvprism roles                         # academic, industry-ds, applied-ai, hydrodynamics, geospatial, + yours
cvprism build --role academic

Each build writes a timestamped folder in vault/build/<role>/ containing:

File What it is cv.pdf Typeset with RenderCV, fitted to the role's page limit cv.docx Plain, ATS-friendly Word file cv.md Markdown evidence.md Every bullet with the cards it cites rejected.md Drafted claims removed because no evidence supported them quality.md Repeated verbs varied, duplicates merged, weak openers or buzzwords to fix ats.md The CV read back like an ATS would: contacts, headings, every line, links, size; plus keyword match for job postings manifest.json Proof for every line and file fingerprints (open spec) cv.rendercv.yaml Editable source for one-off layout tweaks

--no-llm uses your card text directly, with no Claude call.

docs.title: For a specific job posting
docs.text:
cvprism build --jd posting.txt        # or a URL

You also get gaps.md: skills the posting asks for that you have no evidence of, skills with thin evidence, and related evidence you do have. cvprism never adds a skill to your CV without evidence.

docs.title: Your own role
docs.text:
Create roles/<id>.yaml in your vault and inherit from a starter:

v: 1
id: ml-engineer
title: Machine Learning Engineer
extends: applied-ai
vocabulary: [PyTorch, distributed training, inference optimisation]
limits: {pages: 1}
template: sb2nov

Themes: classic, ember, engineeringclassic, engineeringresumes, harvard, ink, moderncv, opal, sb2nov.

docs.title: Mirror the market's language
docs.text:
cvprism market add applied-ai posting1.txt
cvprism market add applied-ai https://example.com/jobs/456
cvprism market extract applied-ai

Phrases that recur in at least 30% of your saved postings are added to the role's vocabulary. They influence which evidence is chosen and how it is worded, never what is claimed.

docs.title: Recruiter-ready by default
docs.text:
• No repetition: two lines never start with the same verb, and lines that say the same thing are merged (the stronger proof wins).
  • No filler: weak openers ("Responsible for", "Worked on") and buzzwords ("passionate", "results-driven") are flagged in quality.md. With Claude drafting, they're forbidden, and lines follow challenge → action → result.
  • ATS read-back: cvprism extracts the text of its own PDF or Word file, like an applicant tracking system, and confirms your name and email are read first, the headings are standard, no line is lost, and proof links survive as text. For job postings, ats.md also scores keyword coverage. It separates skills you have evidence for but didn't include (opportunities) from real gaps.

docs.title: The honesty rule
docs.text: Every bullet must cite at least one card. Every number in a bullet must appear in a cited card's result, a value derived from it (87.5% from 120 → 15 minutes), the card text, or a fact you wrote in profile.yaml. Vague quantities like "dozens" are rejected too. This is enforced by code (ADR-009).
